text.p: Following are key facts on the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum:
- APEC was conceived in 1989 in Australia and started annual summits four years later.

- The first summit was in 1993 in Seattle (host, U.S. President Bill Clinton); the second in Bogor, near Jakarta (Indonesian President Suharto); the third in Osaka, central Japan (then Japanese Prime Minister Tomiichi Murayama); the fourth is in Subic Bay, near Manila (Philippine President Fidel Ramos) on Monday. The fifth will be in Vancouver, Canada, in 1997.

- There are currently 18 members: Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, United States.

- Although a number of countries want to join, no new members will be admitted until 1999. The 1997 summit in Vancouver will fix membership criteria and the 1998 summit in Kuala Lumpur will decide about new members. Countries which want to join include Russia, India, Pakistan, Vietnam, Colombia, Peru and Ecuador.

- The Bogor summit envisioned dropping regional trade and investment barriers by 2020, which would make the grouping the world's biggest and wealthiest free trade zone. The Manila summit is to work out concrete steps to realise the lofty Bogor goal.
- APEC economies account for about 56 percent of the world's economic output and control more than 50 percent of world trade.
- APEC members have about half the world's population.
